content.user_title: Manage Azure App Configuration in Python
content.value_statement: Teams need consistent cloud settings and feature flag workflows. This skill provides Python SDK guidance for Azure App Configuration clients, labels, snapshots, and async access.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install the Azure App Configuration Python package.
Explains connection string and Entra ID authentication patterns.
Demonstrates reading, creating, updating, deleting, and filtering configuration settings.
Covers labels for environment-specific configuration values.
Shows feature flag creation, reading, and listing workflows.
Includes read-only settings, snapshots, and async client examples.
limitations: Requires an existing Azure App Configuration resource and valid credentials.
Focuses on the Python SDK and does not cover other Azure SDK languages.
Does not deploy infrastructure or manage Azure access policies.
Examples need production validation before use with sensitive configuration values.

use_cases.title: Centralize Application Settings
use_cases.description: Build Python service patterns that read settings from Azure App Configuration instead of local files.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Feature Flags
use_cases.description: Create and read feature flags for staged releases, experiments, and controlled production rollouts.

use_cases.title: Prepare Configuration Rollbacks
use_cases.description: Use labels, read-only settings, and snapshots to support safer deployment changes and rollback plans.

prompt_templates.title: Connect a Python App
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new Azure App Configuration client.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to connect a Python app to Azure App Configuration with Entra ID. Include required packages, environment variables, and a minimal read example.

prompt_templates.title: Read Environment Settings
prompt_templates.scenario: Use labels and key prefixes for environment-specific settings.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me read Azure App Configuration settings for a Python service. Use a production label and a key prefix for application settings.

prompt_templates.title: Add Feature Flags
prompt_templates.scenario: Create feature flag guidance for controlled releases.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Python feature flag workflow with Azure App Configuration. Include naming, labels, rollout safety, and how to read enabled status.

prompt_templates.title: Design Production Usage
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced architecture guidance for reliable configuration management.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production pattern for Azure App Configuration in Python. Include labels, feature flags, snapshots, async client use, retries, and secret handling boundaries.

output_examples.input: Request guidance for authenticating a Python service with Azure App Configuration.
output_examples.output: The response explains package installation, Entra ID credentials, the endpoint variable, and a minimal setting read workflow.

output_examples.input: Ask for a feature flag setup plan for a staged production release.
output: Define a clear flag name and production label.
Create the flag in Azure App Configuration.
Read the flag in the Python service before enabling the new path.
Use snapshots or labels to support rollback.

output_examples.input: Ask how to organize settings for development, staging, and production.
output_examples.output: The response recommends labels, key prefixes, read-only production settings, and snapshot creation before deployment changes.

best_practices: Prefer Entra ID authentication for production workloads.
Use labels and key prefixes to separate environments and application domains.
Create snapshots before deployment changes that depend on configuration values.
anti_patterns: Do not store application secrets directly in general configuration values.
Do not print raw production configuration values to shared logs.
Do not use one unlabeled setting set for every environment.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you use the Azure App Configuration Python SDK for settings, labels, feature flags, snapshots, and async clients.

faq.question: Does it require an Azure account?
faq.answer: Yes. You need an Azure App Configuration resource and credentials that can access it.

faq.question: Can it use Entra ID authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes Entra ID examples with Azure identity credentials.

faq.question: Does it manage feature flags?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how to create, read, and list feature flags with the Python SDK.

faq.question: Does it replace production testing?
faq.answer: No. You still need environment-specific validation, access review, and deployment testing.

faq.question: Is it limited to Python?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance focuses on the Azure App Configuration SDK for Python.
